title: Keep verse line breaks everywhere
statement: Show verse in its authored lines wherever it appears, in passages, pictures or films and at any screen width, never joined or re-wrapped, since its line breaks carry meaning.
detail: A poetry and drama unit contrasts blank verse with a rhymed passage and asks why a voice should carry a sentence on past a line break, so its rules bar any visual asset from erasing lineation and keep the full verse lineation visible while a speech is modelled. The book renderer at first did not render verse at all, and the fix added real verse support rather than flattening verse into prose.
against: Not every excerpt keeps its line breaks: a dialogue excerpt in the same unit was kept with "original punctuation and word sequence retained, line wrapping normalized." (grade3-reading/visual-findings-2026-09-07/review-readiness/curriculum-alignment/rebuild/unit9/lesson-07.md, line 3), and the record does not say whether it holds verse.
